A paralyzed American regained mobility in his hands and sense of touch with the help of five chips implanted directly into the brain.

48-year-old Kit Thomas was paralyzed below the chest after a neck fracture. Now he can independently pick up objects and feel sensations again.

Two neuroimplants transmit signals to the muscles bypassing the damaged area of the spinal cord, while three others restore the sense of touch by receiving data from sensors on the skin. The most amazing part is that some restored functions persisted even after the chips were removed.

Another step towards neuroimplants no longer being a fantasy and becoming a common medical practice.

📌 Zcash sets July 28 hard fork to seal Orchard after critical bug 

⚠️ Zcash founder Zooko Wilcox has explained how the network’s July 28 Ironwood hard fork will address uncertainty around a critical flaw in the Orchard shielded pool. The upgrade will not identify or freeze individual counterfeit coins. Instead, it will seal the old pool and limit how much ZEC can leave. 

🔖 Ironwood, also known as NU6.3, is scheduled to activate at block 3,428,143 on July 28. The upgrade will retire the current Orchard pool and introduce a new shielded pool based on the corrected circuit. According to Zcash’s official Ironwood user update, users will no longer be able to send or receive ZEC inside the old Orchard pool after activation. Funds can leave only through the turnstile, which prevents more ZEC from exiting than legitimately entered.

⭐️ The Zcash team said it believes the flaw was “unlikely to have been exploited,” but users cannot independently prove no counterfeit ZEC was created. Ironwood aims to trap any excess value inside the old pool rather than allow it to enter wider circulation. Security researcher Taylor Hornby discovered the Orchard flaw on May 29 while auditing the shielded system. The bug could have allowed an attacker to create counterfeit ZEC inside Orchard without leaving an obvious public record.

🚀 Gala Swap isn't just another DEX. It’s a powerful engine built to capture value directly from market inefficiencies, and it’s fueling a serious opportunity for liquidity providers.

Here’s the breakdown on why this is a potential game-changer, especially for new pools:

The Arbitrage Engine Is Already Running

Let's talk about that brand-new pool you just saw launch. How does it earn anything on day one? The answer is simple: Arbitrage.

The moment a pool goes live, its price can slightly differ from the prices on major centralized exchanges (CEX). Smart traders and automated bots, known as arbitrageurs, are constantly scanning for these tiny gaps. They buy where it’s cheap and sell where it’s dear.

Historical fact: since the early 1990s, Benjamin Netanyahu has been promising that Iran will get the bomb “within 3–5 years.” 

From his 1992 Knesset speech to his 1995 book, from the cartoon bomb at the UN to endless interviews, the deadline keeps rolling while reality stubbornly refuses to cooperate. 

Israeli assessments swing from “by the end of the year Iran will have enough uranium for one bomb” in 2020 to “after the 2025 strikes Tehran has been pushed back two to three years,” but Bibi’s script never changes: “very soon, any day now.”

Campaign fact: in June 2025, the US and Israel hit Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan. Trump stood in front of cameras and declared that Iran’s “nuclear sites are totally and completely destroyed,” that the threat was over — “obliteration” as official branding. 

Months later, US intel and media reports politely walked that back: the program as a whole survived, the clock was set back by months, maybe a year, and significant enriched stock and centrifuges were moved or hidden. 

Before long, familiar estimates reappeared: Iran is roughly 9–12 months from a weapon, if it chooses.
